items.t: Sundrop turns your endless baby photos into recaps, time-lapses and more — without AI
items.d: Sundrop is a new iPhone app that uses Apple's on-device AI to help parents rediscover their favorite photos and create keepsakes without uploading images to the cloud.
items.fullText: New parents take a lot of pictures of their children, but those photos often end up languishing in photo galleries, never to be seen again after the initial snap and share. A new app, Sundrop , aims to make those pictures more useful by turning them into weekly recaps, highlights, time-lapses of the child growing up, and other cute scenes, like putting the child’s photo on a magazine cover or a rookie card. While Google Photos and Apple Photos already provide extensive tools to organize and manage photos, Sundrop is taking aim at a particular niche: Parents with a new baby (usually their first!) who take an overwhelming number of photos and want to do more with those pictures. Image Credits: Sundrop The app was developed over the past few months by the same team behind the read-it-later app, Matter: Ben Springwater, Sky Lan, and Rob Mackenzie (all dads themselves). Notably, Sundrop claims it is designed to be private, and processes all photos locally on the device it is installed on. To make this possible, Sundrop taps into Apple’s Vision framework and on-device Core ML (machine learning) models instead of uploading photos to a cloud server or some other hosted AI service. Both of the child’s parents can use Sundrop together by linking their accounts, which allows the app to sync their shared photos via Apple’s iCloud service. This feature, the company says, means the pictures aren’t sent to any external servers it runs. Image Credits: Sundrop In addition, the team notes that no generative AI is used in the creation of its scenes or highlights. This differentiates it from many photo editing apps on the market, including Google’s, which are increasingly tapping generative AI to create new versions of your photos. Image Credits: Sundrop To find highlights and recaps, Sundrop scans pictures in the parents’ respective Camera Rolls on their iPhones, skipping things like screenshots or duplicates. items.t: Apple TV makes sign language interpretation a built-in accessibility feature
items.d: Apple TV's new accessibility feature lets viewers turn on sign language interpretation within supported titles.
items.fullText: Apple TV is making its content more accessible to Deaf audiences with the launch of a new Sign Language Interpretation feature, the company announced on Tuesday. The feature will initially be available across a limited set of titles, starting this Friday with the release of “ Being Heumann ,” a biopic about disability rights activist Judy Heumann. American Sign Language (ASL) and British Sign Language (BSL) will also be made available for Apple’s hit movie “F1.” Later this year, other titles will follow, including “Way of the Warrior Kid” and “Greyhound.” What makes Apple’s offering different from other platforms is that the sign language version of the film is not a separate product — that is, it’s not a separate film designed just for Deaf viewers. Instead, Apple’s support for sign language is just a setting you enable that’s integrated with the main title, similar to how you could turn on or off closed captions. When a title with the sign language option is playing, an interpreter appears in the bottom right of the screen, translating the spoken words into signs. Apple says it has partnered with a group of DASLs (Directors of Artistic Sign Language) to ensure that the interpreter for each film fits the tone of the film. Notably, the company is not using any AI-generated interpreters, as Apple says that’s not what the Deaf community has said it needs. The feature is shipping in the latest release of iOS 27.2, and can be turned on through a new sign language option in Settings. After being enabled, a new button will appear in the supported Apple Original titles on Apple TV indicating that sign language is available. These titles are labeled with a sign language icon that appears on the title page alongside other features like closed captions or audio descriptions. items.t: Google broadens its AI hardware portfolio with two new specialized chips
items.d: Google's new tensor processing units (TPUs) broaden its chip portfolio to more use cases: confidential model training and more memory capacity.
items.fullText: Google is notching up its chipmaking game as the company seeks to reduce its dependence on chips made by other companies for its cloud computing business. Google on Monday unveiled two new variants of its tensor processing units (TPUs), in-house-developed chips meant for AI workloads, that broaden its chip portfolio to additional use cases: confidential inference and more memory capacity for large workloads. The new units, TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max, are part of the company’s eighth generation of chips introduced in April this year, and build on what those chips offered, which was more inference capacity and support for large training requirements. TPU 8tx, designed with AMD, is based on the TPU 8t chip, and is geared specifically for confidentially training and running AI models, Google said in a blog post. The chip “builds security directly into the hardware layer, keeping sensitive data and model weights protected and isolated even while in active use,” the company wrote. The chip also has a custom inferencing network that lets it run reasoning alongside training, so it can be used to distill and train small models on the fly. That ability, according to Google, could prove useful for cases where a company might want to train a model on its proprietary data without having to move the data between devices. Meanwhile, TPU 8i Max basically combines two of the inference-focused TPU 8i chips the company launched in April, doubling the memory capacity, processing power and bandwidth, but in a single package. The result is a chip that lets AI models handle a larger range of information during queries. The chip launch comes as hyperscalers like Microsoft , Amazon , and even AI labs like OpenAI and Anthropic are working on their own lines of AI-specific semiconductors and accompanying software in order to reduce their reliance on the dominance of Nvidia. items.t: N-able takes its remote access service offline after researcher publishes dozens of zero-day bugs
items.d: The remote access giant also urged its self-hosted customers to take down their own servers amid a "critical security incident," fearing the possibility of cyberattacks.
items.fullText: In Brief Posted: 7:45 AM PST · November 10, 2026 Image Credits: Bryce Durbin / TechCrunch Zack Whittaker N-able takes its remote access service offline after researcher publishes dozens of zero-day bugs Remote access company N-able has confirmed it took down its cloud-hosted offering to fix a slew of security vulnerabilities that were published online this week, giving the company no advance notice to fix them. In a status update on its website, the company said its hosted N-Central offering for customers is now offline “while we take the necessary actions to secure the environments and implement appropriate remediation.” The company also urged customers to take down their own self-hosted deployments of N-Central, fearing that attackers could use the publicly disclosed exploits to hack into customer networks. N-able said during this time customers will not be able to use their N-Central service, which allows corporate customers to remotely access and manage other devices and systems on the same network. Remote access technologies are a frequent target of hackers, as these systems can grant vast access to a company’s network and internal data. Security researcher Ben Bales released the “zero-day” bugs on GitHub on Sunday. In a post on X , Bales dubbed the bugs Able2Shell, describing them as a mix of vulnerabilities capable of stealing credentials, creating new administrative accounts, and gaining root access to affected N-able systems. Bales told Bleeping Computer that he publicly released the bugs as the company allegedly failed to patch the flaws reported in a different product. N-able said that it has no evidence of successful exploitation against any of its customer environments. A spokesperson for the company did not respond to a request for comment about whether it has the ability to check, such as server logs, or if it has no way to check. items.t: Meta’s AI agent Muse lands on Apple Watch and Android Wear OS
items.d: Users can now interact with Meta’s AI assistant through voice calls, text messages, or dictation on their Apple Watch.
items.fullText: Meta is bringing its Muse AI agent to the Apple Watch and Android’s Wear OS, the company announced on Monday. With the launch, users can now interact with Meta’s AI assistant through voice calls, text messages, or dictation directly on their smartwatch. Works around the clock, and now on your wrist. Muse is now on Apple Watch and Wear OS ⌚️ pic.twitter.com/97QRap5XKz — Muse (@Muse) November 9, 2026 The smartwatch launch comes just a month after Meta introduced a dedicated iPad app for Muse. First launched on the App Store in September, the AI assistant’s expansion across Apple devices signals Meta’s growing ambitions for its consumer AI product and its focus on making Muse a central part of its ecosystem. Muse is now one of dozens of consumer-facing AI agents competing for users’ attention. Like many of its competitors, it allows users to connect their accounts to manage email, meetings, bills, and more, while also handling tasks such as booking reservations, ordering groceries, setting goals, and making purchases. Users can also personalize their Muse avatar to their liking and change it into something that resembles a person, an animal, or another type of character. Despite being a relatively new product, Meta has wasted little time introducing new capabilities to Muse. A few days ago, Meta launched Spaces , a new way to communicate and collaborate with Muse. Spaces function as dedicated conversations around specific topics, which Meta describes as “custom experiences” as they’re mini apps that are built on the fly. They appear in the sidebar of the Muse interface and bring up a focused conversation where the AI agent works toward a particular goal on the user’s behalf. Last week, Meta rolled out the ability for users in the U.S. to video chat with their Muse AI avatar. items.t: Aura’s newest e-ink photo frame is even better and more affordable than its last
items.d: Aura is unveiling a new product: a 10-inch digital e-ink frame that can blend in seamlessly with printed photos.
items.fullText: If you’re into interior design, decorating, or just love displaying your family photos, Aura ‘s latest product line will feel magical. Aura’s cordless Ink photo frames have the versatility of a digital photo frame, but their e-ink displays don’t even look digital, blending seamlessly into the rest of your framed photos. A follow-up to its 13-inch, $499 Ink frame , Aura is unveiling a new product that’s a little less pricey: a 10-inch Ink frame that is now on sale for $349. “Ten years ago when we were first starting Aura, we were interested in making an e-ink picture frame. We just wanted a frame that looked like a printed photo and magically changed, but the tech was not there at that point,” Aura co-founder and CTO Eric Jensen told TechCrunch. “So it’s great to be able to see it moving forward.” Aura uses E Ink’s Spectra 6 display for its Ink frames, which can only render six different colors. What sets Aura apart is its proprietary dithering algorithm, a technique that blends a limited color palette into patterns that the eye reads as smooth gradients. How Aura’s dithering algorithm breaks photos down into six e-ink colors Image Credits: Aura While the 13″ Ink frame looks beautiful, it is obvious that the colors are not exact to the original photo. For the new 10″ Ink frame, Aura worked with E Ink on expanding its Spectra 6 technology to incorporate three new proprietary colors: off white, mustard, and orange. “The net effect is that the edges are smoothed a bit more,” Jensen said. “You can see if you zoom in on a face, the places where we would’ve had to previously put white next to red, or something a little more jarring, we can now fill in with the right color, and it effectively makes it a little bit higher resolution.” With the extra three colors, the Ink 10″ is getting truer to representing an original photo, but the colors still appear less satu

items.t: Spotify’s AI DJ gets new voices, personalities, and an option for less chatter
items.d: Spotify Premium users can now customize their AI DJ with new voices with different personalities, or turn off the commentary between songs.
items.fullText: Spotify’s AI DJ, one of the company’s earlier efforts in embracing AI technology to connect people with their favorite music, is getting an upgrade. On Tuesday, the streamer announced that users will now be able to customize their DJ more like they can an AI assistant, by choosing between different voices and personalities. Those who like the feature, but not all the chatter, can also now opt for an experience with less commentary in between sets. Since first launching the AI DJ in 2023 , Spotify has leveraged AI across to improve all areas of its app. Most recently, that has included updates that allow users to chat with a conversational AI agent about music, fine-tune their recommendations with prompts , create playlists with AI, and work with third-party agents like ChatGPT and Claude. However, the DJ remains one of Spotify’s most popular AI features, as it’s used by over 94M Spotify Premium listeners. Now, it’s revisiting one of its first major AI features, taking a cue from the personalization options other AI assistants routinely offer. With the update, Spotify Premium subscribers will be able to choose from an expanded set of AI DJ voices in both English and Spanish. The voices include seven English options with British, American, Irish, Australian, and Indian accents, and two new Spanish options. The different voices will have their own unique personalities as well. For instance, users can pick between three American voices, one of which is laid-back and warm (Casey), another that’s direct and has an edge (Tess), and a third that has a Southern accent and a youthful energy (Lane). In addition to the other various regional accents, there are also two new Spanish voices, one that’s more down-to-earth (Nico) and one that’s more witty and friendly (Fabi). The voices will not replace the AI DJ’s original voice, “X,” which was based on that of a Spotify employee’s real voice recordings. Howeve

items.t: Ring, known for its doorbell cameras, launches a home security drone and an enterprise security robot
items.d: Amazon-owned Ring is pushing into robotics with the launch of a home security drone and a rolling robot designed to patrol and protect businesses.
items.fullText: Ring, the Amazon-owned home security company, is launching its own robotics division, with an eye toward automating security at both the home and the office. The company announced Ring Robotics on Tuesday, debuting two new devices that are sure to stir more than a little bit of controversy. The first new device is a home security drone that users will be able to deploy to patrol their domiciles when they’re out. The other item that the company is launching is a roving enterprise security robot, designed for businesses. First, the drone. Ring calls the device a “flying indoor security camera” — which should give you a pretty good idea of what it’s supposed to do and how it’s supposed to work. Ring Drone Cam is designed to fly from room to room, inspecting what is happening in a user’s house and, if there’s trouble, to alert them. It has been built to integrate with Ring’s other home security devices so, for instance, if a Ring alarm goes off in a particular part of the home (say, the backdoor), the bot will supposedly fly to that location and investigate. When it’s not in use, the drone stays inactive in a docking bay. The drone shoots video in 2K and it also comes equipped with LED lights so that it can keep watch at night and record video in low light. It can be controlled via Amazon’s Alexa Home Map , and the bot can also be scheduled to patrol the house at specific times — so, if you know you’re going to be out for the night or even on vacation, the drone can keep you apprised of what’s happening while you’re away. Now, let’s turn to Ring Rover Cam. Like the drone, this roving robot can be set to patrol specific routes, at specific times, within the user’s business. The robot streams video in continuous 4K, which is viewable via Ring’s mobile app, and a trigger can be set to automatically record if it detects a human. items.t: Cyberattacks threaten to make open-source AI a little less open, Hugging Face exec warns
items.d: Hugging Face executive Irene Solaiman warns that growing cyberattacks on open AI platforms could force tighter security restrictions, threatening the accessibility that makes open-source communities valuable to developers worldwide.
items.fullText: Loading the player… The very qualities that make open AI platforms valuable, like open doors and rich data, might also make them vulnerable to more hacks, Irene Solaiman, chief policy officer and SVP of strategy at Hugging Face said on a recent episode of the Equity podcast. The October attack on OpenCode , which targeted users’ third-party API keys and caused financial damage, is the latest example. It follows an incident this summer in which an OpenAI agent swarm breached Hugging Face in an apparent attempt to cover its tracks after accessing answers to cybersecurity evaluations. The risks aren’t limited to platforms that invite open community contributions. On Monday, AI infrastructure startup Fireworks, which helps developers run and train open AI models, disclosed that attackers had accessed some customers’ model weights, datasets, and billing information. The company temporarily disabled certain self-service dataset functions as it investigates. While the attack isn’t necessarily due to Fireworks’ openness, it highlights how much valuable information is concentrated within AI infrastructure providers. “The things I worry about making an open community targeted are also what makes it special,” Solaiman said on Equity. “We are necessarily permissive. We want the average hobbyist in their basement who doesn’t have an institutional affiliation to be able to contribute.” “You want people to be able to just submit pull requests and allow anybody without a valid affiliation to contribute…but then you have some losers who ruin it for the rest,” she added in a separate conversation. That permissiveness isn’t the only thing drawing attackers. The wealth of information open platforms host also make them targets. items.t: Jensen Huang’s alleged honeypot scandal has inspired some top-notch memes
items.d: Huang publicly confessed to the affair just yesterday, so the internet has the rest of the week to get creative.
items.fullText: Jensen Huang, the CEO and co-founder of the world’s most prominent chip company, has allegedly been honey-trapped by a suspected Chinese spy, and the news has struck the internet like a match to gasoline. Huang has long been seen as a wife guy (or so everyone assumed). He and his wife, Lori, have been together since the 1980s, and both of their children work at Nvidia. Huang has been the closest thing the tech world has to a rock star, with fans lining up for selfies and autographs. Of all the AI overlords, the leather-jacket wearing Huang has seemed like the most level-headed and least erratic, which is why this plot twist has hit so hard . The potential fallout is mind-boggling. Nvidia looms so large over the U.S. stock market that even the company’s domestic drama is a market risk. Countless AI startups depend on Nvidia chips, so any shake-up at the top would ripple far beyond the company. And Nvidia has no publicly disclosed succession plan, so if Huang leaves, it’s unclear who’d take over. Is this how the AI bubble bursts? It’s a question that will be answered in time, but in the meantime, a more pressing matter demands our attention: ranking the funniest memes about the scandal, with bonus points for AI images presumably generated using Nvidia chips. There’s admittedly a lot to choose from, ranging from “500 Days of Summer” jokes to jokes about divorce lawyers to an AI adaptation of the music video for Usher ‘s song “Confessions Pt. II,” a track about cheating. Another person created a viral AI video that re-creates the Coldplay concert where a startup CEO was caught on the Jumbotron hugging a colleague. Huang publicly confessed to the affair just yesterday, so the internet has the rest of the week to get creative.
